bib.title: Meta-Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Model Harnesses

question: Can harness engineering (the code that decides what to store, retrieve and show an LLM) be automated by a search that gives a coding agent full access to prior candidates' code, scores and traces?
hypothesis: Richer access to prior experience (raw traces via a filesystem) beats compressed feedback (scores, summaries, short templates) for harness optimization.
contributions: Meta-Harness, an outer-loop system with an agentic proposer reading code, scores and execution traces of all prior candidates through a filesystem
Gains on online text classification, retrieval-augmented IMO-level math, and TerminalBench-2
Ablation showing raw traces are the key ingredient; practical implementation tips

method.summary: A coding-agent proposer (Claude Code, Opus 4.6) repeatedly inspects a filesystem of every prior harness's source, scores and traces, proposes new single-file Python harnesses, which are validated, evaluated and logged; the Pareto frontier is returned. The base model is frozen and varies by domain.
method.task: automated harness optimization (text classification, retrieval-augmented math, agentic coding)

datasets.name: LawBench (Law)
datasets.split: search set and test set; sizes not stated

datasets.source: OpenMathReasoning, DeepMath-103K, NuminaMath-1.5, PolyMath, Omni-MATH, FineProofs-SFT, AIME 1983-2024, Putnam-AXIOM
datasets.preprocessing: Deduplicated and decontaminated vs eval benchmarks and search set by exact prefix match then Jaccard 0.8; solutions truncated to 5,000 chars; runtime keeps solutions under 4,000 chars, truncated to 3,000 in prompt

datasets.size: 200 problems: 100 IMO-AnswerBench (stratified), 60 IMO-ProofBench, 17 ArXivMath Dec 2025, 23 ArXivMath Jan 2026

datasets.name: TerminalBench-2

other.use: math solvers; GPT-OSS-20B used for search

inference.samples: Math: pass@1 averaged over three samples per problem. Search: single runs, no repeated seeds stated.
inference.prompting: Proposer guided by a minimal domain-specific skill (where to write harnesses, how to inspect history, what files it may edit). Text classification baselines: zero-shot, few-shot N in {4,8,16,32,all}.
inference.retrieval: Math: BM25 with math-aware LaTeX tokenizer, four routes (combinatorics BM25@20 dedup to 8 rerank keep 3; geometry 1 hard NuminaMath ref + 2 BM25; number theory BM25@12 rerank keep 3; default BM25@10 adaptive K). Classification: TF-IDF retrieval of past labeled examples.

parameters.text_classification_search: 20 iterations, 2 candidates per iteration, 40 candidates; population seeded with zero-shot, few-shot, ACE, MCE
parameters.math_search: 40 iterations, 109 candidate harnesses; seeded with zero-shot, few-shot, ACE
parameters.terminalbench_search: 10 iterations (Appendix A run); seeded with Terminus 2 and Terminus-KIRA
parameters.bootstrap: 15-second timeout, /app listing cut to 20 entries, about 80 lines added to Terminus-KIRA
parameters.search_set_size_tip: 50-100 examples in classification, 88 problems for math retrieval

other.wall_clock: a search run completes in a few hours

eval.protocol: Candidates chosen solely on search-set performance; test sets held out until final evaluation of the Pareto frontier. TerminalBench-2 searched and scored on the same tasks, with manual and regex audits for task-string leakage. No seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests stated.

limits: Only one proposer agent (Claude Code with Opus 4.6) tested; authors leave other proposers to future work.
TerminalBench-2 search and evaluation use the same 89 tasks (treated as a discovery problem), so the coding scores are not held out.
Trace-ablation (Table 3) is on one domain with no repeated seeds or significance tests reported.
Bootstrap component has no separate ablation; claimed 2-4 turn saving is asserted.
Per-benchmark breakdown table for math is referred to but not included (App C.3 text says 'When included...').
Authors could not reproduce ForgeCode's 81.8% from public code.
